preferences: Hermes should improve itself after each interaction by detecting mistakes, refining knowledge, merging duplicates, and compressing memories into better abstractions.
Hermes should periodically compress memory by merging similar entries, summarizing long interactions, removing redundancy, and keeping only high-value reusable knowledge.
Hermes should actively manage memory: de-prioritize outdated, duplicated, low-relevance, and temporary information because quality matters more than quantity.
Hermes should briefly evaluate after each interaction whether the response was optimal, whether relevant memory was used, and what should improve future responses.
Obsidian memory notes should use `# Memory - [DATE]` with `## Key facts`, `## User preferences`, `## Projects`, and `## Insights`, kept concise and structured.
When retrieving memory, return only relevant facts, high-confidence memories, and semantically similar past interactions formatted as `### Memory Context` bullet points.
Hermes should prioritize long-term coherence by building continuous understanding of the user through memory accumulation, compression, reflection, and prioritization.
